text:
acme-netops: Hi, hitting TLS client-cert negotiation failures to our Redwood Private control plane after we tightened egress allowlist this morning. Calls to https://private.cp.redwood.acme/api/health immediately fail with 'tls: handshake failure' on our side. No recent config changes on the agent side except the new egress rules. Any ideas?

rina: Sorry you're seeing this. Quick sanity checks: can you paste the openssl s_client output from an agent host? Also which agent/container image + OS?

acme-netops: Running from a test host in the same subnet. Here's the openssl output.

acme-netops: ```
openssl s_client -connect private.cp.redwood.acme:443 -cert client.crt -key client.key -CAfile ca.pem -showcerts
CONNECTED(00000003)
139814024983840:error:14094438:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:ssl handshake failure:s3_pkt.c:1493:SSL alert number 40
---
no peer certificate
---
Certificate chain
<presented nothing>
---
accepting renegotiation
---
closed
```

sam: That looks like the server is dropping the client cert before handshake completes (TLS alert 40). Can you also try with -tls1_2 and with -servername to force SNI?

rina: Also please run a tcpdump to capture the ClientHello/Alert (if allowed). Command: `sudo tcpdump -n -s0 -w /tmp/tls.pcap host private.cp.redwood.acme and port 443` — send capture to us if possible.

acme-netops: Re: SNI, we tried `-servername private.cp.redwood.acme` and `-tls1_2` — same failure. We attached the pcap (sent to the support share).

ops-bot: notice: recent change - customer egress allowlist applied by acme FW team at 06:58 UTC (rule: allow tls to cp.redwood.acme via proxy only).

sam: Two common culprits: 1) corporate TLS inspection/proxy (Zscaler, BlueCoat) doing MITM and not forwarding client certs, or 2) an egress path that terminates TLS at a proxy and doesn't pass through the client certificate to the origin. Do you have a transparent SSL/TLS proxy in front of the egress?

acme-netops: We do have a corporate outbound proxy that performs TLS inspection for most hosts. We thought Private control plane endpoints were on an allowlist that bypasses inspection but maybe the proxy rules changed.

rina: If a TLS-inspecting proxy is present it will present its own cert to the client and then open a new TLS session to Redwood — that will break mutual TLS because the origin never sees the client cert. Two quick checks: 1) `curl -v --cert client.crt --key client.key https://private.cp.redwood.acme/api/health` (see if curl reports a client cert error). 2) `openssl s_client -connect private.cp.redwood.acme:443 -showcerts` from the agent and inspect the server cert issuer — if it's your proxy CA, that's the inspection device.

acme-netops: curl output shows: `SSL: no alternative certificate subject name matches target host name 'private.cp.redwood.acme'` and server cert issuer is `ACME TLS-Inspect CA`. Looks like the proxy is doing MITM.

sam: OK that's consistent. For mutual TLS you need a direct egress path from agent to Redwood control plane (no MITM). Options: - Update firewall/proxy to bypass inspection for the control plane FQDN/IP range and allow raw TCP 443 to pass through, preserving the client certificate, - Configure a TLS passthrough route on the proxy (no termination), or - Terminate mTLS at an edge the proxy can forward certs to (requires support and will need config changes on our side).

support-lead: @acme-netops we'll open a formal escalation. Please provide the following so we can coordinate with eng-sre: 1) full tcpdump pcap, 2) sample agent logs (redwood-agent.log) around 06:50-07:30 UTC, 3) the curl/openssl outputs (you've attached some), 4) the proxy vendor and version and egress rule dump.

acme-netops: Uploaded logs and pcap to the support share. Proxy vendor is 'AcmeProxyCorp v8.2'. Egress rule shows control-plane FQDN allowed but inspection still enabled (we missed bypass).

rina: Thanks. One more debug step for us: can you run openssl from a host that routes outbound directly to the internet (bypass proxy) or from a personal laptop on cellular (if allowed)? If that succeeds it confirms proxy as root cause.

acme-netops: Ran from laptop on cellular, openssl shows full cert chain from Redwood and handshake completes. So proxy is the issue.

eng-oncall: Eng-sre here. Recommending customers do TLS passthrough or add control-plane FQDN/IP to proxy bypass list. Also verifying that our control-plane ALB accepts the client cert OIDs/algorithms your agents use — but since direct connection succeeds that's likely fine.

sam: For mitigation while proxy team works on bypass, you can: 1) configure agents to use an outbound HTTP CONNECT tunnel that disables inspection for those destinations (if your proxy supports bypass for CONNECT), or 2) pin to our dedicated IP ranges and request an explicit FW rule that bypasses inspection, or 3) use a short-term agent proxy config to route control plane traffic via a jump-host that has direct egress.

support-lead: We're assigning P-1 escalation to eng-sre. @eng-oncall can you run a quick check on our edge to confirm we're not accidentally rejecting any client cipher suites?

eng-oncall: On it. Running a live capture and TLS debug on the ALB. Preliminary: ALB received TCP handshake but there were no TLS client certs present from the proxy connection — confirmation of inspection.

rina: TL;DR root cause: corporate TLS inspection/proxy is terminating TLS and not forwarding client certs, causing mutual TLS handshake failure. Next steps for customer: request proxy policy change to bypass the control-plane FQDN/IP range and allow raw TLS passthrough. For us: support team will stay on the call to validate once bypass is in place. :thumbsup:

acme-netops: Thanks all — will push for bypass and update here. Appreciate the quick help.

ops-bot: incident-note: escalation created #INC-2026-1842 by support-lead at 07:35 UTC

support-lead: Marking this thread for follow-up. Please ping if bypass done so we can verify and close the incident. :eyes:
